attributes.action: Make breast cancer and breast health awareness part of Key Stage 4 education
attributes.additional_details: Young people can leave secondary school without basic knowledge of breast and chest health. I believe Key Stage 4 should include age-appropriate education on knowing what is normal, recognising changes and possible signs of breast cancer, how to check yourself, and when to seek medical advice. This should include awareness that breast cancer can affect both women and men, helping young people carry important health knowledge into adulthood.
attributes.background: Require secondary schools in England to teach age-appropriate breast cancer and breast/chest health awareness as part of Key Stage 4 education.

rejection.details:
According to statutory guidance on Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education, all state-funded secondary schools in England are required to cover health protection and prevention, and understanding of the healthcare system. 

Cancer awareness and other specific cancer-related content is already included, such as breast cancer. As part of the ‘Health protection and prevention, and understanding the healthcare system’ topic, secondary school pupils are taught the importance of taking responsibility for their own health and the benefits of regular self-examination and screening.
